title: Wrist and Ankle Pain

rationale.Refer rheumatology: Early aggressive treatment prevents joint damage.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with symmetric polyarthritis involving small joints of hands (MCP, PIP), wrists, and ankles. Morning stiffness >1 hour. Joints are warm, swollen, tender. RA is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory arthritis. Key features: symmetric, polyarticular, involves hands/feet, spares DIP joints (distinguishes from osteoarthritis which involves DIP/PIP, Heberden/Bouchard nodes). Extra-articular: rheumatoid nodules, interstitial lung disease, pericarditis, vasculitis, Felty's syndrome. Labs: RF (rheumatoid factor — 80% sensitive), anti-CCP (anti-citrullinated peptide — very specific >95%), elevated ESR/CRP. X-ray: periarticular osteopenia, joint space narrowing, marginal erosions. Treatment: early aggressive DMARDs — methotrexate first-line. Plus short-term prednisone bridge. If MTX inadequate → add biologic (TNF inhibitor — etanercept, adalimumab). Refer to rheumatology. Physical and occupational therapy.
